ms.report:
Project closeout Video Report
1. Summary of What Was Done
The Wine Supply Chain Tracking & Storage Monitoring System was envisioned as a Proof of Concept (PoC) to explore anchoring a wide range of data elements - static, variable, and high-frequency associated with the wine-producing process onto the Cardano blockchain. The core objective was to ensure data validity and enhance wine traceability, ultimately strengthening end-consumer trust.
Although the project focused on the wine industry, the blockchain integration principles and codebase developed here are applicable to any context where trustworthy data anchoring is required. One direct continuation is our Digital Product Passport (DPP) platform, which extends these concepts to textiles, manufacturing, and other regulated supply chains.
The project demonstrated the technical feasibility of:
・Anchoring high-frequency sensor data via Hydra Layer 2 from distributed storage devices (temperature, humidity, light, etc.).
・Anchoring static and semi-static production data via smart contracts using the CIP-68 token standard.
・Integrating these on-chain components with a lightweight frontend application that captures and renders vineyards, batches, and storage conditions.

We successfully delivered everything committed under this proposal, including a working frontend application integrated with a Cardano smart contract for data anchoring and IPFS for off-chain storage. All code is fully open source, enabling other teams to leverage and extend the assets developed by us.
Beyond the technical scope, this project helped us establish broad connections within both the Cardano ecosystem and the wine sector in Moldova and abroad. Collaboration with wineries and institutions such as ONVV surfaced concrete pain points in data management and compliance reporting.
